title: Nice Words, or True Words as Well? The Interaction Effect Between Upward Ingratiation and Speak-Up Behavior
abstract: Abstract: Employees frequently rely on influence tactics to shape how others evaluate and respond to them. Although prior research has largely examined influence tactics in isolation, little is known about how different tactics operate together to shape workplace relationships and outcomes. Drawing on the warmth–competence framework, we examine the interplay between two commonly used upward influence tactics – ingratiation and speak-up behavior. Using a round-robin, two-wave, multisource survey of employees, leaders, and coworkers across 119 teams in a large metro operating company in China, we tested our hypotheses using multilevel modeling and Monte Carlo simulations. We propose that ingratiation signals warmth, whereas speak-up provides complementary competence and authenticity cues. Consistent with our theorizing, speak-up strengthened the positive relationships of ingratiation with leader trust and coworker respect. Furthermore, the indirect effects of ingratiation on leader-rated promotability through leader trust and on help received from coworkers through coworker respect were stronger at higher levels of speak-up behavior. Together, our findings show how distinct influence tactics provide complementary social information that shapes interpersonal evaluations and workplace outcomes.
